title: Quantile-fused POP selector for latency and network health
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background:
Customers are increasingly sensitive to tail latency and transient network issues across POPs. Current region selection favors single-percentile signals (p95) which sometimes over-prioritizes outlier episodes or misses consistent median shifts. We need a robust POP selector that fuses multiple latency quantiles (p50/p90/p95) with network health signals (packet loss, retransmit rate, control-plane errors) and applies hysteresis to avoid flapping.

Goal:
Build a quantile-fused scoring function and decisioner that: (1) computes a composite POP score from p50/p90/p95 and a normalized network health metric; (2) supports per-tenant tier weighting and model-variant penalties; (3) exposes a deterministic ranking used by the routing layer with graceful fallback to compatible model variants and alternate POPs; (4) is observable and safe to roll out via canary.

Proposal (high level):
1) Telemetry inputs: Prometheus histograms (latency quantiles computed via summaries), synthetic edge probes (ICMP/TCP connect success), and telemetry-derived network health index (0..1) combining packet loss, retransmit %, and control-plane error rate. Aggregation window: rolling 3m and 30m for short-term vs trend.
2) Normalization: Convert quantiles to z-scores relative to POP-specific baseline distributions (maintained by daily job). Network health index is already 0..1 with 1 best.
3) Scoring function: POP_score = alpha * norm(p50) + beta * norm(p90) + gamma * norm(p95) - delta * network_health_penalty + variant_penalty + tier_bias. Weights (alpha,beta,gamma,delta) start as (0.25, 0.35, 0.30, 0.40) and will be tuned in experiments. Lower POP_score == better.
4) Hysteresis and decay: Require a score delta > threshold for T seconds before switching; apply exponential decay on historic baselines to reduce sensitivity to short bursts.
5) Fallback logic: If selected POP's estimated tail latency > SLA or network_health < threshold, fallback order: same-POP compatible smaller variant (quantized), nearest-healthy POP, then degrade to cross-region best-effort. When falling back to a model variant, add a deterministic variant-Rank to preference that preserves model quality preference within the same POP.
6) Determinism & reproducibility: The decisioner must be deterministic given identical inputs (no sampling). Use monotonic tie-breaker on POP id and model id to avoid oscillation.

Implementation scope:
- Score computation service (new microservice: routing-score) reading aggregated telemetry from TSDB (Prometheus remote-write + materialized aggregates in ClickHouse).
- A lightweight policy module in the router that queries routing-score and caches results for 1s (short caching) with fallbacks allowed at request time when network errors observed.
- Baseline maintenance job (daily) to recompute quantile baselines per POP and model family.
- Dashboard: per-POP score timeseries, weight sensitivity slider, canary cohort view, incident drill-down logs.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end test harness with synthetic traffic can demonstrate expected behavior under: increased median (p50), increased tail (p95), degraded network health, and mixed signals.
- No more than 1.5x increase in routing decision rate for the router.
- Canary rollout to 5% of traffic shows no customer-visible error rate increase and p95 within SLA for 95% of canary intervals.
- New metrics emitted: routing_score, routing_decision_reason, fallback_reason, variant_penalty_applied.

Data & dashboards:
- Reference design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/quantile-fused-pop-selector
- Prototype metrics: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/route/quantile-fused-experiment (internal)
- Related PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/834 (early score library), https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/621 (network index export).

Testing & rollout plan:
- Unit tests for normalization, scoring, and tie-breaking (target 95% coverage).
- Integration tests with router simulator (deterministic).
- Staged rollout: feature-flagged canary (5%) -> 20% (48h) -> 100% if no regressions. Add auto-rollback if error-rate or p95 breach thresholds.

Open design trade-offs & questions:
- Weighting strategy: initial weights are heuristic; we should run a retrospective grid-search on 4 weeks of telemetry to pick sensible defaults.
- Baseline frequency: daily baselines may lag fast shifts; consider ephemeral baselines (1h) but risk chasing noise.
- Network health aggregation: should control-plane errors be weighted more than packet loss for certain workflows? Need product input.

Longer-term extensions:
- Incorporate cost signals (eg, cross-region egress) into score for cost-aware routing for low-tier customers.
- Per-tenant tuning: enable tenant-specific weight overrides.
- ML-based scorer replacing linear weights with a small ranker model trained on historical SLA violations.

Notes:
- This ticket intentionally separates scoring and enforcement to reduce router churn and to enable A/B testing with minimal rollout risk.
- Ensure feature flags and runtime knobs are present for fast rollback.
